issue: Can a First Step Act change to § 924(c)'s anti-stacking rule, which applies only prospectively, count as an extraordinary and compelling reason for a compassionate release sentence reduction under § 3582(c)(1)(A)?

sides.position: The § 924(c) anti-stacking amendment cannot be an extraordinary and compelling reason for a sentence reduction, because treating it as one would give the prospective-only change retroactive effect that Congress withheld in the First Step Act.
cases: United States v. Thacker, 4 F.4th 569 (7th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Andrews, 12 F.4th 255 (3d Cir. 2021)
United States v. Rutherford, 120 F.4th 360 (3d Cir. 2024)
United States v. Austin, 125 F.4th 688 (5th Cir. 2025)
United States v. McCall, 56 F.4th 1048 (6th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Crandall, 25 F.4th 582 (8th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Jenkins, 50 F.4th 1185 (D.C. Cir. 2022)
United States v. Black, No. 24-1191 (7th Cir. 2025)

sides.position: The § 924(c) anti-stacking amendment can be an extraordinary and compelling reason for a sentence reduction, at least under U.S.S.G. § 1B1.13(b)(6) for defendants with unusually long sentences who have served at least ten years and face a gross disparity.
cases: United States v. Ruvalcaba, 26 F.4th 14 (1st Cir. 2022)
United States v. McCoy, 981 F.3d 271 (4th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Chen, 48 F.4th 1092 (9th Cir. 2022)
United States v. McGee, 992 F.3d 1035 (10th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Black, No. 24-1191 (7th Cir. 2025)

this_court: The Seventh Circuit departs from Thacker and holds that U.S.S.G. § 1B1.13(b)(6) is a reasonable exercise of the Commission's delegated authority, so the anti-stacking change can support a reduction in qualifying cases. It remands for the district court to exercise its discretion.
quote: We recognize Thacker’s holding that § 924(c)’s anti-stacking amendment cannot constitute an extraordinary and compelling reason for a sentence reduction is not consensus; the courts of appeals have split on the issue.
cite: United States v. Eural Black, No. 24-1191 (7th Cir. 2025)
